newsitem.title: NORWAY: FORECAST - Fokus 1996 profits seen up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Fokus 1996 profits seen up.

text.p: Norway's third largest commercial bank, Fokus Bank ASA, is expected to post 1996 pre-tax profits of about 550 million crowns, up from 429 million crowns in 1995, according to seven analysts polled by Reuters.
The annual result, however, will be inflated by a profit of 107 million crowns from the sale of shares in information technology company Novit AS.
Net interest income, the bank's core business, was seen falling.
One analyst recommended to buy the share, four said hold and the remaining two said sell.

They largely agreed that the share was fairly priced at about 48 crowns. The analyst who issued a buy recommendation said he did not want to miss out on the chance for a higher price in case of a takeover by another bank or a merger.
Financial daily Dagens Naeringsliv said three weeks ago that Fokus would announce annual cost cuts of 80 million crowns when it presents 1996 profits on February 6.
The report said it was probably just a matter of time before Fokus may merge with at least one of three regional commercial banks, Nordlandsbanken, Bergensbanken or Romsdals Fellesbank.
The paper also said it was possible that Fokus Bank might be taken over by Sweden's Svenska Handelsbanken, which it said was aiming for a large share of the Norwegian market.
